newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts BNL, ups Napoli.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts BNL, ups Napoli.

text.p: on Friday issued the following two statements.
BANCA NAZIONALE DEL LAVORO RATINGS DOWNGRADED
London: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has removed Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro ("BNL") from RatingWatch with negative implications and downgraded its Long-term rating from A+ to A.

The Individual rating has also been downgraded, from C/D to D while the Short-term and Legal ratings are unchanged at A1 and 2 respectively. Over the past five years, BNL has set down a new commercial strategy, tightened management controls and streamlined its business lines to become a more unified, "universal" bank.

The acquisition, together with INA, of around 60% of Banco di Napoli's shares should allow BNL to decrease its reliance on the interbank market and reduce loan concentration by reaching a wider client base.
However, BNL still has to make substantial investments in IT systems and procedures and also needs to make further progress in rationalising its corporate structure, which remains complicated.

Furthermore, the quality of the group's loan book is still rather weak, with around 12% of total loans, net of reserves, impaired at end-1996. Profitability, although improving, remains low by domestic and international standards and the low level of reserve coverage of problem loans may continue to impact negatively on net income.
There are also likely to be additional costs relating to the acquisition of BdN shares.

Following the transfer of Artigiancassa in 1996 from the Italian Treasury, the group's capitalisation reached satisfactory levels and with a EU total capital ratio, at end-1996, of 9.82%, of which 7.76% was tier 1.

London: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has upgraded Banco di Napoli's Short-term rating to A2 from A3, its Long-term to BBB+ from BBB, and its Individual to D/E from E. The Legal rating of 2 has been affirmed. The bank's ratings have been removed from RatingWatch with positive implications.
Control of Banco di Napoli (BdN) has been acquired by Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) and INA as their purchase of 60% of BdN's shares from the Italian Treasury has now been completed.
INA and BNL have undertaken to strengthen BdN's capital position by injecting ITL 1,300 bln of new capital, which will enable BdN to comply with regulatory capital requirements.
Following large losses, and its major restructuring, BdN reported a small profit for the first quarter of 1997, and expects to breakeven at year-end.
Almost all its doubtful loans have been transferred to a special vehicle, SGA, which is effectively guaranteed against losses by the Banca d'Italia, and will not be consolidated by BdN.
In addition, as a result of its loan loss experience, BdN has substantial tax benefits. We are therefore raising the bank's ratings as above.

IBCA's Legal and Individual Ratings for Banks Legal ratings deal with the question of whether an institution would receive support either from owners or governmental authorities if it ran into difficulties. While we consider the Legal rating to be a prime factor in the assessment of credit risk, IBCA's Individual ratings permit an evaluation divorced entirely from any consideration of outside support: "If the bank were entirely independent and could not rely on support from state authorities or its owners, how would it be viewed?".
